breakfast.name: Laplap (Root Vegetable Cake)
instructions: Grate root vegetable into paste
Spread on banana leaves
Add coconut cream
Add island cabbage or meat
Wrap and bake over hot stones 2 hours
breakfast.description: Vanuatu's national dish — grated root vegetable baked in banana leaves.

breakfast.name: Boiled Yam with Coconut
instructions: Boil yam until tender
Serve with coconut cream

breakfast.name: Simboro (Banana Leaf Wrapped Pudding)
instructions: Simboro is the Vanuatu banana pudding wrapped in leaves -- a staple across Melanesia
Grated banana or plantain mixed with coconut cream and greens
Wrapped in banana leaves and cooked in an earth oven (umu) or steamed
The banana leaf imparts a subtle grassy flavor
A traditional morning meal or any-time food
Melanesian cuisine relies heavily on banana, coconut, and root vegetables
breakfast.description: Vanuatu banana leaf pudding -- simboro, grated banana or plantain mixed with coconut cream and island cabbage, wrapped in banana leaves and cooked in an earth oven. Melanesian cuisine relies on banana, coconut, and root vegetables. A traditional morning meal.

breakfast.name: Tuluk (Meat-Stuffed Banana Dumpling)
ingredients: Bananas or manioc (grated, forms the dough)
Filling: corned beef or tuna, onion
instructions: Tuluk is the Vanuatu stuffed dumpling -- grated banana or manioc around a meat filling
The starch (banana or manioc) is grated and forms the outer shell
Filled with tinned corned beef or tuna -- canned goods are important in Pacific Island diets
Wrapped in banana leaves and cooked in the umu (earth oven) or boiled
Tinned meat became a Pacific Island staple during and after World War II
A hearty meal eaten for breakfast or lunch
breakfast.description: Vanuatu stuffed dumpling -- tuluk, grated banana or manioc shell around a corned beef or tuna filling, wrapped in banana leaves and cooked. Tinned meat became a Pacific Island staple during and after World War II. A hearty meal.

breakfast.name: Cassava Porridge
instructions: Cassava porridge is a Melanesian breakfast -- grated cassava cooked with coconut cream
Cassava (manioc): one of the primary root crops of the Pacific
Grated and cooked into a thick porridge with coconut cream
Simple, filling, and nutritious -- a pre-work breakfast
Cassava must be properly prepared (soaked/cooked) to remove cyanogenic compounds
breakfast.description: Melanesian breakfast porridge -- grated cassava cooked with coconut cream until thick and creamy. Cassava is a primary Pacific root crop. Simple and filling. Must be properly prepared to remove natural cyanogenic compounds.

lunch.name: Tuluk (Meat in Root Vegetable)
instructions: Mix meat with onion
Wrap meat in grated taro
Wrap in banana leaves
Bake or steam 60 min
lunch.description: Meat wrapped in grated taro and banana leaves.

lunch.name: Fish in Coconut Milk
instructions: Simmer coconut milk with onion
Add fish, cook 15 min
Squeeze lime

lunch.name: Lap Lap (National Dish)
ingredients: Root vegetable: yam, taro, manioc, or breadfruit (grated into a paste)
Meat: chicken, pork, or flying fox (fruit bat -- traditional)
instructions: Lap lap is the national dish of Vanuatu -- grated root vegetable baked in an earth oven
A root vegetable (yam, taro, manioc, or breadfruit) is grated into a fine paste
The paste is layered with coconut cream, meat, and greens on banana leaves
Cooked in an umu (earth oven): a pit lined with hot stones
The result: a dense, starchy cake infused with coconut and smoke
Different islands use different root vegetables -- each island has its version
Flying fox (fruit bat): a traditional protein in Vanuatu and other Melanesian islands
Lap lap is cooked for celebrations, feasts, and everyday meals
The earth oven cooking is communal -- preparing the umu is a group effort
lunch.description: Vanuatu national dish -- lap lap, grated root vegetable (yam, taro, manioc, or breadfruit) layered with coconut cream and meat on banana leaves, cooked in an umu (earth oven lined with hot stones). Each island uses different roots. Communal umu preparation. Flying fox (fruit bat) is a traditional protein.

lunch.name: Coconut Crab
ingredients: Coconut crab (Birgus latro -- the world's largest land arthropod)
instructions: The coconut crab is the world's largest land arthropod -- found across the Pacific Islands
Can grow over 1 meter leg span and weigh 4+ kg
Called "robber crab" because it steals shiny objects
The meat is rich, dense, and tastes faintly of coconut (from the crab's coconut diet)
Simply boiled or steamed and served with coconut cream
A delicacy -- increasingly protected due to overharvesting
The crab cracks open coconuts with its powerful claws -- hence the name
lunch.description: Vanuatu delicacy -- coconut crab (the world's largest land arthropod, 1m+ leg span), meat rich, dense, and faintly coconut-flavored from the crab's coconut diet. Simply steamed with coconut cream. Increasingly protected due to overharvesting. Cracks open coconuts with powerful claws.

lunch.name: Island Fish Curry
instructions: Island fish curry reflects the colonial-era introduction of curry powder to the Pacific
Fresh reef fish cooked in coconut cream with curry powder
British and French colonial influence (Vanuatu was jointly ruled as the New Hebrides)
The coconut cream base is Melanesian; the curry powder is colonial import
A common everyday lunch across Vanuatu
Fresh fish is abundant -- the islands are surrounded by rich coral reefs
lunch.description: Vanuatu fish curry -- fresh reef fish in coconut cream with curry powder (colonial-era import). British and French jointly ruled as the New Hebrides. Melanesian coconut base meets colonial curry. Fresh fish is abundant from surrounding coral reefs.

lunch.name: Bougna (New Caledonian-style Parcel)
instructions: Bougna is the New Caledonian version of the earth oven parcel -- also made in Vanuatu
Protein and root vegetables wrapped in banana leaves with coconut cream
Cooked on hot stones in an earth oven
Similar to lap lap but with larger chunks of ingredients rather than grated
The French colonial presence in New Caledonia influenced naming but not the technique
The Melanesian cooking technique shared across Vanuatu, New Caledonia, and Fiji
lunch.description: Melanesian earth oven parcel -- bougna, chicken or seafood with root vegetables and coconut cream wrapped in banana leaves, cooked on hot stones. Shared technique across Vanuatu, New Caledonia, and Fiji. Larger chunks than grated lap lap.

dinner.name: Island Stew
instructions: Brown meat
Add vegetables and coconut milk
Simmer until tender
dinner.description: Simple coconut stew with island vegetables.

dinner.name: Grilled Fish
instructions: Score, season, grill over coals

dinner.name: Umu Feast (Earth Oven Whole Pig)
ingredients: Root vegetables: yam, taro, sweet potato, manioc
instructions: The umu feast is the Vanuatu earth oven celebration -- a whole pig and root vegetables
A pit is dug, filled with volcanic stones, and heated by burning wood
When the stones are white-hot, the food is placed on top, wrapped in banana leaves
The pit is covered with earth and banana leaves -- sealing in the heat
The food slow-cooks for 3-4 hours in the enclosed steam
An umu feast marks celebrations: weddings, funerals, grade-taking ceremonies
The Melanesian feast tradition: communal cooking, communal eating
In Vanuatu, the umu is called a "laplap oven" -- it's the same technique used for the national dish
dinner.description: Vanuatu earth oven celebration -- umu feast, whole pig and root vegetables placed on white-hot volcanic stones in a pit, covered with banana leaves and earth, slow-cooked 3-4 hours. Marks weddings, funerals, and ceremonies. Communal Melanesian cooking and eating tradition.

dinner.name: Kumala Stew (Sweet Potato Stew)
ingredients: Kumala (sweet potato -- Pacific Islands variety, purple or orange)
instructions: Kumala is the Pacific Islands name for sweet potato -- a dietary staple
Sweet potato was brought to the Pacific from South America -- evidence of ancient Polynesian contact with the Americas
The kumala in Vanuatu: boiled, mashed, or made into stew with coconut cream
A simple dinner -- kumala and coconut cream with protein
The sweet potato sustained Pacific Island populations for centuries
dinner.description: Vanuatu sweet potato stew -- kumala (the Pacific name), stewed with coconut cream and chicken or tuna. Sweet potato was brought from South America -- evidence of ancient Polynesian trans-Pacific contact. The staple that sustained Pacific Island populations for centuries.

dinner.name: Natapoa (Seafood in Coconut)
ingredients: Fresh seafood: fish, octopus, or shellfish
instructions: Natapoa is Vanuatu-style seafood in coconut -- similar to Polynesian oka or ika mata
Fresh raw seafood "cooked" in lime juice (the acid denatures the proteins -- ceviche technique)
Mixed with fresh coconut cream, onion, and chili
The coconut cream rounds out the citrus acidity
A no-cook preparation -- ideal for tropical islands without kitchen infrastructure
The freshness of the seafood is everything -- caught that day
dinner.description: Vanuatu raw seafood in coconut -- natapoa, fresh fish or octopus "cooked" by lime juice (acid denatures protein, like ceviche), mixed with coconut cream, onion, and chili. Similar to Polynesian oka. No-cook preparation ideal for tropical islands. Freshness is everything.

dinner.name: Roasted Breadfruit with Coconut Fish
instructions: Breadfruit roasted whole over coals -- the skin blackens and the interior steams
The roasted flesh is dense, starchy, and slightly nutty
Served with fresh fish in coconut cream
Breadfruit is a staple crop across the Pacific -- a single tree can feed a family
The breadfruit tree was what the HMS Bounty was transporting when the mutiny happened (1789)
Eaten as a dinner with coconut-braised fish
dinner.description: Vanuatu roasted breadfruit with coconut fish -- whole breadfruit charred over coals (skin blackens, interior steams), served with fish in coconut cream. A single breadfruit tree can feed a family. The HMS Bounty was transporting breadfruit trees during the 1789 mutiny.

snacks.name: Nangai Nut
instructions: Crack open, eat raw or roasted

snacks.name: Nalot (Pounded Breadfruit)
instructions: Nalot is pounded breadfruit -- a staple across Melanesia and Polynesia
Breadfruit roasted over coals or boiled until soft
Pounded with a wooden pestle until smooth and sticky
Mixed with coconut cream
Breadfruit: a starchy tree fruit that Captain Bligh attempted to transport from Tahiti (the HMS Bounty mutiny, 1789)
A filling, portable food eaten as a snack or side
snacks.description: Vanuatu pounded breadfruit -- nalot, breadfruit roasted and pounded smooth with coconut cream. Breadfruit: the starchy tree fruit Captain Bligh tried to transport (HMS Bounty mutiny, 1789). A filling, portable Melanesian staple.

snacks.name: Coconut Bread
instructions: Coconut bread is a common baked good across the Pacific Islands
A simple quick bread made with coconut cream or grated coconut
Introduced by missionaries and colonial bakers who brought flour and ovens
Sweet, moist, and coconutty
Baked in wood-fired ovens on many islands
Reflects the blending of Western baking with Pacific Island coconut culture
snacks.description: Pacific Island coconut bread -- simple quick bread made with coconut cream or grated coconut. Introduced by missionaries and colonial bakers who brought flour and ovens. Sweet, moist, and coconutty. Western baking meets Pacific Island coconut culture.

snacks.name: Taro Chips
instructions: Taro chips are the Pacific Island equivalent of potato chips
Taro sliced thin and fried in coconut oil until crispy
Taro: the ancient Melanesian root crop -- cultivated for thousands of years
Starchier and denser than potato -- the chips are heartier
Sold at markets and roadside stands
snacks.description: Pacific Island taro chips -- taro root sliced thin and fried crispy in coconut oil. Taro is the ancient Melanesian root crop cultivated for thousands of years. Starchier and denser than potato chips. Sold at markets and roadside stands.

imageCredit.author: No machine-readable author provided. Thierry Caro assumed (based on copyright claims).

snacks.name: Island Popcorn (Popped Sago)
instructions: Sago starch popped in hot coconut oil -- the Melanesian popcorn
Sago: the starch extracted from sago palm trunks
When dropped in hot oil, the starch puffs like popcorn
Seasoned with salt or sugar
A simple snack made from locally available starch
Sago is a traditional starch source across Melanesia and Southeast Asia
snacks.description: Melanesian popcorn -- popped sago starch, puffed in hot coconut oil and seasoned. Sago is starch extracted from palm trunks, a traditional Melanesian and Southeast Asian starch source.

desserts.name: Simboro (Banana Pudding)
instructions: Mash bananas with coconut
Wrap in banana leaves
Steam 60 min

desserts.name: Vaivai (Coconut Pudding)
ingredients: Tropical fruit (banana, mango, papaya -- for topping)
instructions: Vaivai is Vanuatu coconut pudding -- a thick, creamy coconut dessert
Coconut cream thickened with tapioca starch and sweetened
Set into a pudding and topped with fresh tropical fruit
Simple -- relies on the quality of the coconut
Fresh coconut cream is squeezed from grated coconut flesh -- not from a can
A celebration dessert and everyday sweet
desserts.description: Vanuatu coconut pudding -- vaivai, thick fresh coconut cream sweetened and thickened with tapioca, topped with tropical fruit. Relies on the quality of the coconut. Fresh cream squeezed from grated coconut flesh, not canned.

desserts.name: Banana Fritters
instructions: Banana fritters are made across the Pacific wherever bananas grow
Mashed ripe banana mixed with flour and sugar, spooned into hot oil
Fried until golden and caramelized
The many banana varieties in Vanuatu provide different flavors and textures
Vanuatu has dozens of banana cultivars -- more banana diversity than almost anywhere on earth
desserts.description: Vanuatu banana fritters -- ripe bananas mashed with flour and fried golden. Vanuatu has dozens of banana cultivars -- more banana diversity than almost anywhere on earth. Each variety provides different sweetness and texture.

desserts.name: Tapioca Pudding with Coconut
instructions: Tapioca pudding with coconut cream -- a common Pacific Island dessert
Tapioca pearls (from cassava starch) cooked in coconut milk until translucent
The pearls become chewy and translucent -- each one a small burst of texture
Sweetened with sugar, flavored with vanilla or pandan
Topped with fresh tropical fruit
Tapioca: originally from South America, brought to the Pacific via Southeast Asia
desserts.description: Pacific Island tapioca pudding -- small tapioca pearls cooked in coconut milk until translucent and chewy. Originally from South America, brought to the Pacific via Southeast Asia. Topped with fresh tropical fruit.

desserts.name: Manioc (Cassava) Cake
instructions: Cassava cake baked or steamed in banana leaf-lined pans
Grated cassava mixed with coconut cream and sugar, pressed flat and baked
Dense, chewy, and sweet -- the cassava creates a unique gummy texture
A common celebration sweet across Melanesia and Southeast Asia
The cassava and coconut combination is fundamental to Pacific Island desserts
desserts.description: Vanuatu cassava cake -- grated cassava mixed with coconut cream and sugar, baked or steamed in banana leaf-lined pans. Dense and chewy with a unique gummy texture. The cassava-coconut combination is fundamental to Pacific Island desserts.

drinks.name: Kava
instructions: Pound kava root
Mix with water
Strain through mesh
Serve in coconut shells at nakamal
drinks.description: Kava — the heart of Ni-Vanuatu culture, drunk every evening at nakamals.

drinks.name: Coconut Water
instructions: Crack open, drink

drinks.name: Kava (Nakamal Drink)
ingredients: Kava root (Piper methysticum -- fresh, pounded or ground)
instructions: Kava is the ceremonial and social drink of Vanuatu -- and the country's most important cultural tradition
Kava: the root of the Piper methysticum plant, pounded or chewed and mixed with water
The effect: a mild sedative and muscle relaxant -- calming, numbing, and peaceful
The taste: earthy, peppery, and mouth-numbing -- acquired taste at best
Drunk at nakamals (kava bars) every evening across Vanuatu
Traditionally a men's drink -- drunk at separate nakamals
The kava ceremony: drinking in silence, spitting after swallowing, sitting in contemplation
Vanuatu has the strongest kava varieties in the Pacific -- "two-shell kava" can be very potent
Kava is central to ni-Vanuatu identity -- it is to Vanuatu what wine is to France
drinks.description: Vanuatu's most important cultural tradition -- kava, the root of Piper methysticum pounded and mixed with water. Mildly sedative, calming, mouth-numbing. Drunk at nakamals (kava bars) every evening. Vanuatu has the strongest varieties in the Pacific. Central to ni-Vanuatu identity like wine is to France.

drinks.name: Fresh Coconut Water
ingredients: Young green coconut (the husk still green, the water inside clear and sweet)
instructions: Fresh coconut water is the most natural drink in the Pacific Islands
Young green coconuts hacked open with a machete -- the water is sipped directly
Naturally isotonic -- better than any sports drink for rehydration
After drinking the water, the soft jelly-like flesh inside is eaten with a spoon made from the husk
Coconut palms line every beach in Vanuatu -- the "tree of life"
The coconut provides water, cream, oil, flesh, fiber, and wood -- every part is used
drinks.description: Pacific Island natural drink -- fresh young coconut water, hacked open with a machete and sipped directly. Naturally isotonic. After drinking, the soft jelly-like flesh is eaten with a husk spoon. The coconut palm is the "tree of life" -- every part is used.

drinks.name: Lemon Leaf Tea
instructions: Lemon leaf tea is a common Pacific Island herbal infusion
Fresh lemon tree leaves steeped in hot water
Fragrant, citrusy, and calming
Traditional medicine: used for stomach complaints and relaxation
Grown in every Vanuatu garden -- no import needed
drinks.description: Pacific Island herbal tea -- fresh lemon leaves steeped in hot water. Fragrant, citrusy, and calming. Used in traditional medicine for stomach complaints. Grown in every Vanuatu garden.
